absent: Internal validation of the checked scheduler setters beyond delegation is not shown.
Layouts of run queue, task structure, scheduling class, affinity context and wait queue heads are not shown.
No-hz kick handling, balancing algorithm and stats reset behavior are not shown.
Bandwidth enforcement, period handling and ratio use are not shown.
Numeric values of capacity scale, clamp bucket count, nice bounds and real time priority limits are not shown.
Security hook, capability and ownership check internals are not shown.
Deadline and fair parameter helper internals are not shown.

findings.text: Affinity context flags are distinct bit values with check at one, migrate disable at two, migrate enable at four and user at eight.

Bandwidth scaling uses shift twenty with unit as one shifted by that amount, ratio shift eight, maximum bit width as sixty four minus shift, and maximum bandwidth as one less than two raised to that width.
Migration batch bound has two build variants with values eight and thirty two.
No-hz kick bit positions are zero through three for balance, stats, new idle balance and next, with single bit kick values derived from each position and a mask combining balance, stats and next.
Scheduler statistics report version is seventeen.
Scheduler parameter update sentinel meaning retain existing policy is negative one.
Utilization clamp bucket spacing is the capacity scale divided across the bucket count with rounding to nearest.
Interrupt time accounting record holds total accumulated time, tick delta, start timestamp and a sequence synchronization object for sixty four bit counters.
Scheduler change context carries a priority value, a task pointer, a scheduling class pointer, integer flags and two booleans indicating queued and running state.
Acquiring two spin locks orders them by address with lower first then takes the second with single depth nesting annotation.
Raw spin lock pair acquisition uses address ordering and nested annotation, while paired release unlocks each lock in turn.

Releasing two run queue locks distinguishes shared versus distinct underlying locks, releasing the second only when distinct and otherwise performing a nominal release annotation before releasing the first.

Two-lock scoped guard facility provides a constructor taking two locks plus cleanup attributes and a with-style declaration that arranges automatic unlock of each on scope exit, with a raw spinlock instantiation for run queue pairs.
Simple wait queue operations serialize list and state changes under the queue raw spin lock with interrupt save or disable variants, including wake paths and prepare and finish paths.
Affinity read path holds the task pi lock with interrupt save while under read side protection, and statistics domain traversal holds read side protection across the domain walk.
Fair schedulability test reports runnable exactly when the fair queued count on the run queue is positive.
Stop task placement always keeps the task on its current processor and never migrates.
Stop balance outcome mirrors whether the stop entity is runnable on that run queue.
Stop wakeup preemption, tick handling and current update are empty because the stop entity is never preempted and has no tick work.
Stop selection returns no task when not runnable and otherwise returns the run queue stop pointer, while next-task setup records execution start from the run queue task clock.
Stop enqueue and dequeue adjust the run queue running count by one and dequeue reports success.
Stop previous-task handling updates common current execution accounting.
Process lookup by identifier returns current for zero and otherwise looks up by virtual identifier, while the acquiring variant holds read protection and takes a reference when found.

Parameter installation retains old policy under the sentinel, dispatches deadline or fair helpers by policy, clears timer slack for real time or deadline and restores the default when leaving them, then stores real time priority and recomputes normal priority and load weight.
Task priority helper subtracts maximum real time priority from static priority and idle lookup returns the idle pointer of the named processor run queue.
Core idle test reports idle when core scheduling is enabled and current equals idle, otherwise it defers to the generic idle processor test.

Statistics display prints version and tick timestamp for the header, per-processor run queue counters and delay totals, then per-domain spans and per-idle-type balancing counters plus active balance and remote wake counters.

Attribute copy zeroes the destination, treats zero size as version zero default, rejects sizes outside version zero to page size with size feedback and too-big error, requires version one size for clamp flags and clamps nice into range.
Parameter extraction reports deadline details for deadline tasks, real time priority for real time tasks, and nice plus slice for other tasks.
Common yield routine locks the local run queue, counts the yield, invokes the donor class yield operation, unlocks with preemption control and then schedules.
Module exposes simple wait queue init, single wake, full wake, exclusive prepare, event prepare with signal check, and finish operations.
Module exposes scheduler policy setters that forward to internal checked setters, including fifo secondary with mid range real time priority and normal with supplied nice value.
Module exposes affinity set and get, task priority derivation, idle task lookup and core idle determination.
Module exposes a direct yield helper that marks current running before delegating to the common yield path.
Nice entry clamps the increment and resulting nice into allowed bounds, rejects lowering without permission, applies the security hook and then updates user nice.

Setscheduler entries validate policy non-negativity and parameter presence, copy from user, look up and reference the target, then delegate, with setparam using the retain-policy sentinel and setattr handling keep policy and keep params flags.

Get scheduler returns policy with reset-on-fork adjustment, getparam returns real time priority or zero, and getattr returns policy, flags, class parameters and clamp values with size negotiation and dynamic deadline flag validation.

Set affinity validates the target, rejects no-setaffinity tasks, checks ownership or capability, applies the security hook, stages the user mask and delegates with the user flag, while get affinity validates length and alignment and returns the active intersected mask.
Yield entry delegates to the common yield path and reports success.

Statistics sequence starts with a header record at offset zero then iterates online processors in order, mapping each to a cookie value and ending with null beyond the last processor, with next incrementing the offset and stop doing nothing.

Exclusive prepare always joins the queue and sets the requested state, event prepare checks pending signals first and on signal detaches and reports a restart error instead of joining, and finish marks running and detaches only if still linked.
Stop class defines yield, class switch and priority change as impossible transitions, with priority change allowed only when the value is unchanged.
Full wake drains the wait list into a temporary list and wakes each waiter, dropping and retaking the queue lock between waiters when more remain.
Yielding, switching to, or changing priority of stop tasks is treated as a fatal programming error.

Undersized clamp requests and out-of-range attribute sizes fail validation, user copy faults propagate as fault errors and missing targets as search errors, and invalid policy or pid values are rejected.
Affinity changes without ownership require nice capability in the target user namespace and pass security hooks, while length checks reject too-small or misaligned user buffers.
